name: TX-30
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's +25 Democratic partisan lean after redistricting
Haynes's large fundraising edge and $200k outside support
model.rationale: The district's strong Democratic lean plus Haynes's decisive financial advantage and near-certain market pricing leave no evidence pointing toward an upset, so the forecast stays at a Safe D margin near the district's fundamentals.
model.watch: Any late polling or unexpected outside spending on Jackson's side would be the first sign the margin could tighten.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Dallas-area TX-30 is an open seat after redistricting drew a heavily Democratic district, with a partisan lean of about +25 points Democratic. Frederick Haynes III, the Democratic nominee, has raised over $420,000 and holds roughly $120,000 on hand, supplemented by about $200,000 in outside support. Republican Everett Jackson has raised under $18,000 with minimal cash remaining.

No public general-election polls cover the race, and no expert raters have issued ratings, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and money. Prediction markets give the Democrat roughly a 96% chance of winning. The combination of the district's lean, the fundraising gap, and market pricing points to a comfortable Democratic hold.
